messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — streaming-completions: p99 latency spike > 20s observed in us-west-2 (region). Affected service: streaming-completions-v1. Trigger: p99_latency > 20s for 3m.
maya: acknowledging, paging on-call. I see degraded streaming in our dashboard too. tagging @liam who is on-call.
liam: on it. can someone drop the prom query for p95/p99 and active streaming stalls? starting triage.
infra-bot: metrics snapshot attached (last 10m):
```
# prometheus
sum(rate(streaming_requests_total{region="us-west-2",status="ok"}[1m])) by (node)
max_over_time(streaming_latency_p99{region="us-west-2"}[5m])
```
infra-bot: detected anomalous GPU events on nodes: gpu-az2-17, gpu-az2-18 — correctable ECC errors (CE) spike and thermal_throttle_count increase.
liam: reading node logs now. pulling `dmesg` from gpu-az2-17: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Corrected ECC error
[ 12346.001234] thermal: gpu0: throttling event temp=92C
[ 12347.112233] svc: streaming-worker[pid=2345] stall detected: kv-cache wait > 12000ms
```
liam: summary — ECC CE spikes correlate with p99 spikes; thermal throttle events at same times. might be flaky GPU causing long stalls in attention kernels.
maya: customer impact — Product reported increased latency and partial stream truncation for several sessions. Sophie, do we have open support tickets from top customers?
sophie: AcmeChat and BrightDesk have raised issues. drafting status update for customers — proposed text: "We are investigating increased end-to-end streaming latency in us-west-2; routing changes and mitigation in progress. No data loss reported." Want an RTO estimate?
liam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Migrate new streaming requests away from affected AZ using runtime routing (route policy => avoid gpu-az2). 2) Trigger fallback to smaller non-quantized model variant for active sessions if stall > 10s. 3) Drain / cordon affected nodes for further debug. 
ben: I can kick the routing change. running command: `rwctl routes set --region us-west-2 --avoid-nodes gpu-az2-17,gpu-az2-18`
deploy-bot: rolling routing change started. will take ~30s to switch traffic.
liam: also enabling experimental prefix-KV cache bypass to reduce long-held locks: `config set streaming.kv_lock_timeout_ms 2000` (temp).
ahmed: I see a burst of CPU fallback tasks — cost will increase if we keep fallback longer than necessary. track and annotate customer billing impact.
maya: Jordan, you're next on-call in 10m — I'll handoff once we stabilise. Please prepare to run hardware diagnostics if we confirm ECC hardware faults.
jordan: got it. ping me when drain starts; I'll kick off vendor ticket if ECC continues after warm reboot.
infra-bot: cordon initiated on gpu-az2-17; live migration of pods started. Evacuation timeline: ~120s per pod for graceful streaming handoff.
liam: noticed one streaming stall case where session reconnected and resumed after fallback model — logs show `attention_kernel OOM-retry` on the GPU prior to stall. attaching snippet.
```
E ATTENTION_KERNEL: launch failed - resource temporarily unavailable
I RETRY_KERNEL: attempt 1
W KV_CACHE: lock wait 15000ms
```
liam: hypothesis — repeated correctable ECCs are causing driver retries which increase kernel latency and eventually thermal events which throttle clocks, amplifying p99.
sophie: Customer-facing update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating latency spikes in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes or on resolution." :thumbsup:
maya: current impact — p95 still within SLO but p99 is ~18-26s depending on node; streaming stalls reduced after routing change but not fully resolved for historical sessions pinned to nodes.
liam: next steps — keep cordon, drain remaining pods from gpu-az2-18 as well, collect hardware logs and nvml dumps, and if CE count persists after reboot escalate to supplier. Also create an internal incident ticket (ENG-XXXX) for postmortem.
jordan: taking ownership for hardware follow-up. I'll schedule reboots during low traffic window and coordinate vendor remote diagnostics.
ben: monitoring shows error rates decreasing after cordon but a handful of sessions still see tail latency > 10s due to reconnects.
maya: ok planning handoff — liam, leave a short runbook in the incident thread with commands you ran and investigator notes. Jordan will own the hardware ops and postmortem. Sophie will keep customers updated.
liam: runbook snippet: 
```
# quick mitigation
rwctl routes set --region us-west-2 --avoid-nodes gpu-az2-17,gpu-az2-18
kubectl cordon gpu-az2-17
kubectl drain gpu-az2-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
nvml-smi --query-ecc-errors --format=csv > /tmp/ecc-gpu-az2-17.csv
collectd export metrics to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/us-west-2/3400001111/
```
liam: logging handoff: I'm available for questions but shifting to advisory. Jordan will escalate if ECC persists after warm reboot.
jordan: acknowledged — will run `nvml-smi --reset-ecc` where supported, otherwise schedule full reboot. Also open vendor ticket ID VND-90817.
amend: (typo fix) ahmed: billing note added to incident: track CPU-fallback hours and customer credits potential.
maya: we stabilized customer-visible impact. continuing monitoring for 2 hours. postmortem owners: infra/hw (jordan), runtime (liam), customer comms (sophie). Action items assigned. :ambulance:
pagerduty-bot: incident P1 resolved (mitigation) — escalation cleared.
maya: thanks team. we'll convert this to a postmortem and include kernel traces, nvml dumps, and timeline. please add any missing context to ENG-XXXX.
